content.title: About
content.content: Butter replacement powder (4921) is a dry product made from vegetable oils, emulsifiers and stabilizers. When reconstituted with water it forms a creamy spread that mimics the taste and texture of regular butter. It is used in cooking, confectionery and food manufacturing as an alternative to traditional butter.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The powder is easy to transport and store because it does not require refrigeration.
It is a popular ingredient in vegan recipes, being completely plant‑based.
Properly reconstituted, it retains a buttery flavor without the typical oil aftertaste.
The powder allows precise dosing, simplifying calorie control in dishes.
Unlike solid butter, the powder has a much longer shelf life.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Most of the fats are poly‑ and monounsaturated, making it more heart‑friendly than regular butter.

items.title: Cholesterol‑free
items.content: Being plant‑derived, it contains no cholesterol.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Formulations often include added B2 and B12, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Easy to digest
items.content: The powdered form hydrates quickly and is gentle on the digestive system.

items.title: Supports dietary restrictions
items.content: Suitable for vegans, lactose‑intolerant individuals and anyone avoiding dairy.

items.title: Allergy to plant ingredients
items.content: The product may contain soy, sunflower or other allergens; check the label if you have sensitivities.

items.title: Additive content
items.content: Some versions include flavor enhancers and preservatives that may not be suitable for sensitive stomachs.

items.title: May not fully replace butter in baking
items.content: Differences in fat crystal structure can require recipe adjustments for optimal texture.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Mix 1 tsp of powder with 8–10 ml of water, whisk until a smooth creamy consistency is achieved. The resulting spread can be used on bread, in sauces, creams, baked goods and for sautéing. Increase the powder‑to‑water ratio for a firmer texture if needed.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in a sealed container in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. Shelf life is typically 12–18 months. After opening, use within 3 months and protect from moisture.

cheeseburger-on-wheat-bun-1-large-patty.title: Cheeseburger on Wheat Bun with Large Patty

content.title: About
content.content: A cheeseburger is a classic fast‑food item consisting of a wheat bun, a large beef patty (about 150 g) and melted cheese. The patty is grilled or pan‑fried, and the bun is often lightly toasted. Common additions include lettuce, tomato, onion, pickles and various sauces.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first cheeseburger was served in the United States in the 1920s.
A wheat bun gives a softer texture compared with the traditional sesame‑seed bun.
A 150 g patty is considered a “super‑size” portion and is common in fast‑food chains.
Cheese melts at around 70 °C, creating the characteristic stretchy layer.
Cheeseburgers are typically served with french fries and a soft drink.

items.title: Protein source
items.content: The beef patty provides high‑quality animal protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Iron content
items.content: Red meat is rich in heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.

items.title: Calcium from cheese
items.content: Melted cheese adds calcium, important for bone and teeth health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Meat and cheese supply B12, B6, and niacin, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Energy dense
items.content: A cheeseburger provides a quick source of calories, useful for high‑energy needs.

items.title: High calories and fat
items.content: The large patty and cheese make the cheeseburger calorie‑dense and high in saturated fat; moderation is advised.

items.title: Sodium
items.content: Salt in the bun, sauces, and cheese can contribute to elevated blood pressure if consumed in excess.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Cheese may trigger allergic reactions in individuals with lactose intolerance or milk protein allergy.

items.title: Potential meat pathogens
items.content: Undercooked patty may harbor bacteria such as E. coli or salmonella; cook to an internal temperature of at least 71 °C.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cheeseburgers are typically eaten by hand, holding the bottom of the bun. Add sauces, vegetables, or extra toppings to taste. The patty can be swapped for turkey or a plant‑based alternative if desired.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Best consumed immediately. If needed, store in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours in an airtight container. Reheat in an oven or skillet, toasting the bun separately to keep it from becoming soggy.

content.title: About
content.content: Corn chips, plain (Fritos) are crunchy corn snacks without added flavors or spices. They are made from whole‑grain corn flour, water, vegetable oil and salt, then fried until golden. The product is popular as a stand‑alone snack and as a base for Mexican‑style dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Fritos were first introduced in 1932 by The Frito Company in Texas.
Corn chips are made from whole‑grain corn flour, giving them a denser texture than potato chips.
The original recipe contains no artificial colors or flavorings.
Fritos are commonly used as a base for nachos and taco salads.
In the United States, plain corn chips rank among the top‑selling snack items in the no‑flavor category.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Corn chips provide complex carbs that supply sustained energy and help keep you feeling full.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Whole‑grain corn contributes a modest amount of fiber that supports digestive health.

items.title: Provides iron
items.content: Corn contains non‑heme iron, which contributes to hemoglobin formation.

items.title: Low in sugar
items.content: Unlike many sweet snacks, these chips contain virtually no sugar.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Corn supplies thiamine (B1) and niacin (B3), which are important for energy metabolism.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: The salt used in production can contribute to elevated blood pressure if consumed in excess.

items.title: Calorie density
items.content: Chips are energy‑dense; portion control is recommended to avoid over‑consumption.

items.title: Corn allergy
items.content: A small number of individuals may be allergic to corn products.

items.title: Trans fats (depending on oil)
items.content: If partially hydrogenated oil is used for frying, trans fats may be present, which are detrimental to heart health.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Corn chips can be enjoyed straight from the bag, added to salads, used as a base for nachos with cheese, guacamole or salsa, and incorporated into Mexican dishes such as tacos and chili.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep chips in a sealed container in a cool, dry place. For longer shelf life, store them in the refrigerator to prevent oil oxidation.

content.title: About
content.content: The egg salad sandwich on wheat bread is a classic light lunch or snack. Whole‑wheat bread provides a soft, slightly crunchy base, while the egg salad—made from boiled eggs, mayonnaise, mustard, and seasonings—adds a creamy, savory flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Egg salad became popular in the United States in the early 20th century as a convenient sandwich filling.
Wheat bread is often chosen over white bread for its higher fiber and B‑vitamin content.
Traditional recipes include finely chopped eggs, celery, and dill for extra aroma.
The sandwich packs well in plastic wrap, making it a favorite office lunch.
Variations may add avocado, spinach, or a light yogurt‑based dressing instead of mayo.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Eggs provide high‑quality protein essential for tissue repair and muscle maintenance.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Both wheat bread and eggs supply B12, riboflavin, and niacin, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Source of healthy fats
items.content: Mayonnaise or alternative spreads contribute monounsaturated fats that can support heart health in moderation.

items.title: Fiber
items.content: Whole‑wheat bread adds dietary fiber, aiding normal digestion.

items.title: Vitamin D and choline
items.content: Eggs are a good source of choline, important for brain function, and contain a modest amount of vitamin D.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to eggs, ranging from mild to severe anaphylaxis.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Mayonnaise and bread add calories; portion control is advisable for calorie‑restricted diets.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: Eggs contain cholesterol; people with elevated cholesterol levels should consume them in moderation.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Wheat bread contains gluten, making the sandwich unsuitable for those with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The sandwich is easy to eat by hand, preferably cut in half. It can be served cold or lightly toasted. Add lettuce, tomato, or cucumber slices for extra freshness.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the assembled sandwich in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. If the bread begins to dry out, wrap it tightly in plastic. Keep the egg salad separate if you need longer storage.

nutritional-powder-mix-protein-light-nfs.title: Nutritional powder mix, protein, light, NFS

content.title: About
content.content: Nutritional powder mix, protein, light, NFS (5497) is a high‑quality blend of plant‑based proteins enriched with vitamins and minerals. The product is designed to support muscle recovery, boost energy, and conveniently supplement the diet. The powder dissolves easily in water, milk, or plant‑based drinks without clumping and has a light flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The blend contains pea, rice, and hemp proteins, providing a complete amino acid profile.
Enzyme‑probiotic complexes are included to enhance nutrient absorption.
The product is free from gluten, lactose, and artificial sweeteners.
A light formula is specially developed for athletes monitoring calorie intake.
Packaging is made from recyclable material to reduce environmental impact.

items.title: Supports muscle growth
items.content: A rich protein composition promotes muscle‑fiber synthesis after workouts.

items.title: Improves recovery
items.content: B‑vitamins and magnesium help accelerate the body’s restorative processes.

items.title: Boosts immunity
items.content: Added vitamin C and zinc enhance the immune system’s defenses.

items.title: Reduces fatigue
items.content: Electrolytes (potassium, sodium) maintain fluid balance and lessen feelings of tiredness.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Probiotics and dietary fiber promote a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Allergy to plant proteins
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to pea or soy components.

items.title: Excessive protein intake
items.content: Very high protein consumption can strain the kidneys, especially in people with pre‑existing conditions.

items.title: Interaction with medications
items.content: High magnesium levels may affect the efficacy of certain drugs, such as antibiotics.

items.title: Additive sensitivity
items.content: The product contains no artificial sweeteners, but those with specific sensitivities should use caution.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Mix one scoop (≈30 g) of powder with 250 ml of water, milk, or a plant‑based beverage. For extra flavor and texture, add fruit, berries, or nuts. Consumption is recommended immediately after training or as a nutritious snack between meals.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the powder in a cool, dry place, tightly sealed. Keep moisture and direct sunlight away. For long‑term storage (over 6 months), it is advisable to keep it in the refrigerator.

content.title: About
content.content: Spaghetti squash is a variety of winter squash whose flesh separates into strands that resemble spaghetti when cooked. Boiling, baking, or steaming softens the flesh, creating long, noodle‑like fibers with a mild, slightly sweet flavor and very low calorie content.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The name comes from the pasta‑like texture of the cooked fruit.
It belongs to the Cucurbitaceae family and is native to North America.
Raw fruits can weigh 1–3 kg, but lose about half their weight after cooking.
The seeds are edible after roasting and are a good source of healthy fats.
Spaghetti squash is popular in low‑carb and gluten‑free diets as a pasta substitute.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: One hundred grams of cooked spaghetti squash provides roughly 20 kcal, making it ideal for weight management.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Dietary fiber supports digestion, promotes satiety, and helps maintain gut health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains vitamin B6 and niacin, which are important for metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Rich in carotenoids (beta‑carotene) and vitamin C, which combat oxidative stress.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Provides potassium, magnesium, and manganese, essential for blood pressure regulation, muscle function, and metabolism.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Although uncommon, some individuals may be allergic to cucurbit vegetables.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: Raw seeds and skin contain oxalates, which can contribute to kidney stone formation if consumed in excess.

items.title: Overeating
items.content: Large portions may cause gastrointestinal discomfort due to the high fiber content.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cooked spaghetti squash can be served as a pasta alternative with tomato sauce, pesto, vegetable ragù, or in casseroles. It also works well in salads, soups, and Asian‑style noodle dishes. Drizzle with olive oil and season with salt, pepper, or herbs before serving.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store raw squash in a cool, dry place for up to 2–3 weeks. After cooking, keep it in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 4 days. Freeze cooked strands in freezer bags for longer storage (up to 3 months).

content.title: About
content.content: Trail mix with chocolate is a blend of dried fruits, nuts, and pieces of dark or milk chocolate. This mix combines crunchy nuts, sweet dried fruit, and aromatic chocolate, providing a quick source of energy and a pleasant taste.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Trail mixes were originally used by climbers and hikers as a lightweight, nutritious snack on the trail.
Chocolate in the mix is often coated with nuts, which reduces sugar crystallization and extends shelf life.
The combination of nuts and dried fruit delivers a wide range of vitamins and minerals, including potassium, magnesium, and vitamin E.
In many countries trail mixes are sold in single‑serve packets, convenient for gyms and offices.

items.title: Energy support
items.content: Carbohydrates from dried fruit and healthy fats from nuts quickly replenish glycogen stores and sustain endurance.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Chocolate, especially dark, provides flavonoids, while nuts supply vitamin E, helping protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Cardiovascular support
items.content: Monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fats in nuts help lower LDL cholesterol levels.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Both dried fruit and nuts are high in fiber, promoting healthy digestion.

items.title: Muscle‑supporting minerals
items.content: Magnesium and potassium found in nuts and dried fruit aid muscle function and nerve signaling.

items.title: Tree‑nut allergy
items.content: The mix may contain peanuts, almonds, cashews, or other nuts that can trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Dried fruits and chocolate add significant sugar, which may be problematic for diabetics or those watching sugar intake.

items.title: Calorie density
items.content: Trail mix is calorie‑dense; portion control is advisable, especially on weight‑management diets.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Some versions include salted nuts; people monitoring sodium should choose unsalted options.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Trail mix with chocolate is convenient as a standalone snack, or can be added to yogurt, oatmeal, or smoothies. It also works well in baked goods such as granola bars or as a topping for desserts.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in an airtight container in a cool, dry place away from direct light. For longer storage keep it in the refrigerator to prevent nut oils from going rancid and chocolate from melting.
